title: Name tags
prompt: The office prints a name tag for everyone, and names were typed by hand in all sorts of case. Write `solve(employees)` so it returns `employee_id` and `name_tag`.
rules: `name_tag` is the first name, one space, then the last name, with no spaces at the start or end of either.
Each word starts with a capital letter and the rest is lower case: `aNNA de la CRUZ` becomes `Anna De La Cruz`.
If one of the two names is missing, the tag is the other name alone. Return one row per employee, with only these two columns.
hints: `F.trim` removes the spaces around a value and `F.initcap` gives each word a capital first letter and lower-cases the rest.
Tidy each name on its own, then join them with a space.
`F.concat` gives `NULL` when any part is missing. `F.concat_ws(" ", ...)` skips the missing part instead.
starter:
from pyspark.sql import functions as F


def solve(employees):
    # Return employee_id and name_tag.
    return employees
explanation: Standardize each name, then join them: `F.concat_ws(" ", F.initcap(F.trim("first_name")), F.initcap(F.trim("last_name")))`, selected next to `employee_id` with `.alias("name_tag")`. `trim` removes the stray spaces at the ends, so the tag never has two spaces in the middle or one at the start. `initcap` capitalizes the first letter of every word and lower-cases the rest, which fixes `SILVA` and `de la cruz` alike. `concat_ws` is the right join here because it skips a missing part, so someone with no last name still gets a tag; `F.concat(first, F.lit(" "), last)` would give `NULL` for them.
